answers.why: Capture skill's entry: command lookup, repo rules file, who; nothing in the reader's rules or skills queues work mid-task.
Capture's one-exchange procedure ("Queued." then back to the task); no reader rule or skill does this, and it asks before queueing ("never queue without their say-so"), so it breaks no reader rule.
Part of capture: queue and claim work before the first edit; it matches the reader's scope rule rather than fighting it.
Capture's Rescue session procedure; works with the plugin's meow queue and has no reader counterpart.
Capture's riffing mode (one-line replies, "Nothing is built, merged, dropped or released on a reply nobody read"); nothing like it in the reader.

The herd skill's body; its model default ("on opus") applies to sessions the plugin starts, not to a subagent dispatch, so reader engineering rule 6 does not govern it, and it gates paid starts on the owner's say-so.
Associate role file of the herd skill; routes work by declared domain, which the reader has no equivalent of.
Opening of the herd skill's handoff role: when a session hands off; part of a working skill the reader lacks.
Handoff steps for the retiring session; it leaves clone removal to the owner ("only on their go-ahead"), consistent with reader safety rule 1.
Handoff steps for the session that stays; part of the herd skill, no reader counterpart.
Handoff steps for the new session; part of the herd skill, and its branch naming does not touch main.
Fixed chat lines for handoff steps, part of the herd skill's handoff role.
Reviewer role opening of the herd skill: an independent reviewer whose verdict binds; the reader has no review-pair skill.
Reviewer setup step of the herd skill; a template that works when the plugin fills it in.
Reviewer's per-review procedure (fetch commits, run tests, attack, accept or reopen); the reader's release-notes skill does nothing like it.
Reviewer limits: no editing the worker's code, "Never use `--force`"; consistent with reader safety rules.
Reviewer stop rules; it never stops its own pair and leaves clone cleanup to others, in line with reader safety rule 1.
Reviewer's rigor: build checks (cite file:line, watch the test fail); part of the herd skill, and the test-fails point restates reader engineering rule 3 inside a working skill.
Worker role of the herd skill: claim, branch, hand in, wait for the verdict; pushes only to item branches, never to main.

Builder checks of the herd skill (paste raw output, "Blocked is a real answer"); its five coding rules mostly repeat reader engineering rules 1, 2 and 5, and it defers to the project's own debt marker.
Opening of the herder voice skill; only wraps the persona.
Switch for the Cat Herder cat voice, a persona setting.
Cat names and voice lines, persona text.
Cat-voice wording of capture confirmations, persona.
One voice line for retirement, persona.
Cat-voice handoff lines, persona.
Euphemism rules for the cat voice, persona.
Queue skill: set up, find the command, field-trip phone rules, voice-reading of dictated messages; asks before setup and "Never `init` over it", and the reader has no queue skill.
Queue skill's working procedures (claim, review, reorder, move, groom); "Never use `--force` on your own" agrees with reader safety rules, and nothing in the reader does this work.
Queue skill's Overheard block format for relaying another session's words; part of a working skill the reader lacks.
A sample ledger entry used as an example, not an instruction.
Queue skill's question ledger ("A question the owner skipped is unread, not answered"); agrees with reader safety rule 5 and adds a procedure the reader lacks.
The /meow command: runs one quoted meow call and shows its output; it works as shipped and the reader has no command like it.
